mainTopic: Vows with improper conditions, and the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל over סמיכה on offerings brought on יום טוב.
overview: This amud opens by finishing ריש לקיש's question to רבי יוחנן. Someone vowed to be a נזיר but wanted to pay for his offerings with מעשר שני money. רבי יוחנן answers that the vow stands but the improper add-on does not work: 'נדור ואינו יוצא; נזיר ואינו מגלח.' רב פפא then rules on a man who said 'Give 400 זוז to so-and-so, and let him marry my daughter.' Because the gift came first, the man takes the money whether or not he marries her. Next, a ברייתא learns from 'כמשפט' that an obligatory עולה needs סמיכה. רבי יצחק בר אבא says this must follow בית שמאי, but the גמרא shows that בית הלל could also need that פסוק, because they learn obligatory שלמים from two sources combined (אתיא מבינייא). The גמרא then cites two תנאים who disagree about what בית שמאי and בית הלל actually argued over: סמיכה itself, or its timing right before the שחיטה. Finally, a ברייתא tells how הלל הזקן quietly brought his עולה on יום טוב, how בית שמאי gained the upper hand that day, and how בבא בן בוטא stepped in to protect בית הלל's view. His story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Can a נזיר pay for his offerings with מעשר שני money?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש finishes his question to רבי יוחנן: if someone says 'הריני נזיר, and I will shave using מעשר שני money,' what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: '…and I will shave with second-tithe money.' What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a question that began on the previous amud. A person accepted נזירות but tried to pay for his end-of-נזירות offerings with מעשר שני money, and ריש לקיש asks what happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר who finishes his term shaves his head and brings offerings. Those offerings are a new obligation, so they must be paid for with ordinary money, not with מעשר שני money that is already set aside for eating in ירושלים. The question is whether the vow falls apart because of this improper condition, or whether the vow stands and only the condition is cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who vowed to avoid wine, haircuts, and contact with the dead
'And I will shave.' Here it means bringing the offerings that come with the shaving at the end of נזירות
Second tithe, produce or money that must be used for food in ירושלים
'What is it?' The standard way of asking what the law is

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the second half of a question. It starts earlier with 'הריני נזיר.' Before that, ריש לקיש asked a parallel question: 'I will bring a תודה and fulfill my חגיגה obligation with it.' The answer in the next step covers both questions.

phrases.english: and I will shave [i.e., bring my nazirite offerings] with second-tithe money: what is the law?
phrases.notes: The beginning of the question, 'הריני נזיר,' comes earlier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues ריש לקיש's question earlier; this is the נזיר version of the earlier תודה/חגיגה question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the vow of נזירות take effect, and does the condition about מעשר שני money work?

steps.title: The vow stands, but the improper condition does not work
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the vow takes effect, but the improper add-on is ignored. The person bringing the תודה does not fulfill his חגיגה obligation, and the נזיר cannot use מעשר שני money for his offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He is bound by his vow, but he does not fulfill his obligation [of חגיגה with the תודה]. He is a nazirite, but he does not shave [using second-tithe money].
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers both of ריש לקיש's questions with one rule: the vow counts, and the improper condition is simply dropped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the תודה case, the person must still bring the תודה ('נדור'), but it does not count as his חגיגה ('ואינו יוצא'). In the נזיר case, he is a full נזיר ('נזיר'), but he cannot pay for his offerings with מעשר שני money ('ואינו מגלח'). The key idea is that the main commitment stands and the add-on that conflicts with הלכה is cut off.

keyTerms.meaning: He is bound by his vow; the vow takes effect
And he does not fulfill his obligation
And he does not shave, meaning he may not bring the offerings in this improper way

steps.whatToRemember: An improper condition does not cancel the vow. The vow stands and the condition falls away.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the theme of the rest of this passage: when part of a statement works and part does not, the working part survives. The next case, about giving money and marrying a daughter, builds on this idea.

phrases.english: He said to him: He is bound by his vow, but he does not fulfill [his חגיגה obligation].
phrases.notes: This answers the earlier תודה/חגיגה question.

phrases.english: He is a nazirite, but he does not shave [with second-tithe money].
phrases.notes: This answers the נזיר question here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 1 and the earlier parallel question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The vow takes effect, and the condition that conflicts with halacha is not honored.

steps.title: Four hundred זוז and marrying the daughter
steps.stepSummary: A man instructed: 'Give 400 זוז to so-and-so, and let him marry my daughter.' רב פפא rules that the recipient takes the money and may choose whether to marry her.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man said to them: 'Give four hundred zuz to so-and-so, and let him marry my daughter.' רב פפא said: He takes the four hundred, and as for the daughter, if he wants he marries her, and if he wants he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related case where a statement has two parts, and רב פפא decides that only the first part is binding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man said the gift first ('give him 400') and only afterward mentioned marriage. So the gift was already complete, and the marriage was just a wish or suggestion added on, not a true condition of the gift. That is why the recipient keeps the money no matter what he decides about marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain man; the usual opening of a story
Give him
זוז coins
And let him marry my daughter
He takes

phrases.english: There was a certain man who said to them:

phrases.aramaic: הַבוּ לֵיהּ אַרְבַּע מְאָה זוּזֵי לִפְלוֹנִי,
phrases.english: Give four hundred zuz to so-and-so,
and let him marry my daughter.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אַרְבַּע מְאָה — שָׁקֵיל,
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: The four hundred, he takes;
and his daughter: if he wishes, he marries her;
if he wishes, he does not marry her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a case with a similar idea: when a statement has two parts, the first part can stand on its own even though the second part does not bind.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the gift is stated first, the recipient takes the money and is not obligated to marry the daughter.

steps.title: Word order decides whether it is a condition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that רב פפא's ruling depends on the gift being said first. If the man had said 'let him marry, and give him,' then the money depends on the marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that he said 'give him and let him marry.' But if he said 'let him marry and give him,' then if he marries, he takes the money, and if he does not marry, he does not take it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind רב פפא's ruling and shows when the outcome would be different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whatever is said first is the main point. If the gift comes first, it is a full gift. If the marriage comes first, the gift is a reward for marrying, so it becomes a real condition. The same words in a different order can change the law.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is; often introduces a precise inference from a ruling
But if he had said
He marries

steps.whatToRemember: 'Give him and let him marry' means the money is a free gift. 'Let him marry and give him' means the money depends on the marriage.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the marriage is always irrelevant. It becomes a binding condition when it is mentioned first.

phrases.english: The reason is that he said 'give him and let him marry,'

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אִי אָמַר לִנְסֵיב וְהַבוּ לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: but if he said 'let him marry and give him,'
if he marries her, he takes [the money];
and if he does not marry her, he does not take it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from רב פפא's ruling based on word order.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the marriage is stated before the gift, the money depends on the marriage.

steps.title: מרימר teaches the ruling as his own
steps.stepSummary: מרימר taught the ruling 'נדור ואינו יוצא' in his own name, without saying who first taught it.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרימר sat and stated this teaching in his own name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story. It sets up the next step, where רבינא comments on how this teaching should be passed on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'This teaching' refers back to the ruling about attaching an improper condition to a vow, such as the תודה/חגיגה case. מרימר presented it as a plain ruling without naming its source.

keyTerms.meaning: He sat (and taught)
A teaching or halachic ruling
In his own name

phrases.english: Mareimar sat and was saying this teaching
in his own name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the vow ruling from step 2 to discuss its source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מרימר stated the ruling without attributing it to anyone.

steps.title: רבינא: we learn it as ריש לקיש's question to רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבינא tells מרימר that in his tradition, this ruling is taught as ריש לקיש's question to רבי יוחנן and רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to מרימר: You teach it this way. We teach it as the question that ריש לקיש asked רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא points out a different tradition for the same teaching. It is not a plain ruling, but a question and answer between two great אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא does not disagree with the law itself. He corrects the source and form of the teaching. In his tradition, the ruling belongs to רבי יוחנן, in answer to ריש לקיש's question, which is how the גמרא presented it just before.

keyTerms.meaning: You teach it this way
We
He asked him
We teach

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how carefully the חכמים tracked who said a teaching and in what form. A ruling that comes from רבי יוחנן's answer to ריש לקיש carries that authority.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Mareimar:
You teach it this way;
we teach it as the question that

phrases.aramaic: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מַתְנִינַן לַהּ.
phrases.english: Reish Lakish asked of Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to מרימר's unattributed version by giving the attributed tradition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ruling is taught as רבי יוחנן's answer to ריש לקיש's question.

steps.title: A ברייתא: an obligatory עולה needs סמיכה, learned from a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites before רבי יצחק בר אבא that the words 'כמשפט' teach that an obligatory עולה follows the rule of a voluntary עולה and needs סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught in front of רבי יצחק בר אבא: 'And he brought the burnt-offering and did it according to the rule.' This means according to the rule of a voluntary burnt-offering. It teaches that an obligatory burnt-offering also needs סמיכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that uses a פסוק to show that an obligatory עולה needs סמיכה. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that a voluntary עולה (עולת נדבה) needs סמיכה. The ברייתא reads 'כמשפט' ('according to the rule') as saying that an obligatory עולה follows that same rule. So the ברייתא assumes that without this פסוק, we would not know that an obligatory עולה needs סמיכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaning one's hands with force on the head of an offering before it is slaughtered
A voluntary burnt-offering, brought by choice
An obligatory burnt-offering, one a person is required to bring
'According to the rule', meaning the standard procedure
It requires

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק itself (ויקרא ט:טז) is about the עולה that אהרן brought when the משכן was inaugurated. That was an obligatory עולה. This is why the word 'כמשפט' is read as 'like the rule of the voluntary one.'

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: A tanna taught before Rabbi Yitzchak bar Abba:
"And he brought the burnt-offering
and did it according to the rule"
meaning: like the rule of a voluntary burnt-offering.
This teaches about an obligatory burnt-offering
that it requires leaning of the hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new section. It goes back to the topic of סמיכה from the משנה, not to the רבי יוחנן and רב פפא discussion in steps 2-6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An obligatory עולה needs סמיכה. This is learned from 'כמשפט', which compares it to a voluntary עולה.

steps.title: רבי יצחק says this ברייתא must follow בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר אבא says the ברייתא follows בית שמאי. בית הלל learn obligatory offerings from voluntary ones, so they would not need a פסוק for this.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The one who told you this, whose view is it? It is בית שמאי, who do not learn obligatory שלמים from voluntary שלמים. If it were בית הלל: since they do learn obligatory שלמים from voluntary שלמים, an obligatory עולה also should not need a פסוק. They could learn it from a voluntary עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק בר אבא identifies whose view the ברייתא follows. He says it can only be בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the סוגיא, בית הלל learn the rules of obligatory שלמים from voluntary שלמים, and בית שמאי do not. By the same logic, בית הלל could learn the obligatory עולה from the voluntary עולה, so they would not need 'כמשפט'. Only בית שמאי, who refuse that kind of comparison, would need a special פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is it?
They learn (one case from another)
Obligatory peace-offerings, such as the חגיגה
Voluntary peace-offerings
It should not need a פסוק

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that whether something needs its own פסוק depends on how freely you allow comparisons between categories. The ברייתא is therefore tied to one side of the בית שמאי and בית הלל debate.

phrases.english: He said to him: The one who told you this, whose view is it?
It is Beit Shammai,

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא גָּמְרִי שַׁלְמֵי חוֹבָה מִשַּׁלְמֵי נְדָבָה.
phrases.english: who do not learn obligatory peace-offerings from voluntary peace-offerings.
For if it were Beit Hillel,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּגָמְרִי שַׁלְמֵי חוֹבָה מִשַּׁלְמֵי נְדָבָה,
phrases.english: since they learn obligatory peace-offerings from voluntary peace-offerings,

phrases.aramaic: עוֹלַת חוֹבָה נָמֵי לָא תִּבְעֵי קְרָא,
phrases.english: an obligatory burnt-offering also should not need a verse,
since they would learn it from a voluntary burnt-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דַּאֲמַר לָךְ מַנִּי — בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the ברייתא in step 7 by saying whose opinion it follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא that needs a פסוק for סמיכה on an obligatory עולה follows בית שמאי, not בית הלל.

steps.title: Maybe בית הלל learn obligatory שלמים from obligatory עולה instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבי יצחק's assumption. Maybe בית הלל learn obligatory שלמים from obligatory עולה, and the obligatory עולה itself still needs a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do you know that בית הלל learn obligatory שלמים from voluntary שלמים? Perhaps they learn them from an obligatory עולה. And the obligatory עולה itself needs a פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק's claim. It suggests a different source for בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק's argument works only if בית הלל compare 'obligatory to voluntary'. But maybe they compare 'obligatory to obligatory': obligatory שלמים learned from obligatory עולה. In that case, the obligatory עולה still needs its own פסוק ('כמשפט'), and the ברייתא could follow בית הלל too.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where (do you know)?
Perhaps
Itself

phrases.english: And from where do you know that Beit Hillel
learn obligatory peace-offerings from voluntary peace-offerings?
Perhaps they learn them from an obligatory burnt-offering,
and the obligatory burnt-offering itself needs a verse.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִמַּאי דְּבֵית הִלֵּל שַׁלְמֵי חוֹבָה מִשַּׁלְמֵי נְדָבָה גָּמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind רבי יצחק's statement in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's assumption that בית הלל learn obligatory שלמים from voluntary שלמים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is another possible source: obligatory עולה. That source still needs a פסוק, so the ברייתא could fit בית הלל as well.

steps.title: Rejected: an obligatory עולה is just as different as voluntary שלמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Voluntary שלמים are different because they are common, but an obligatory עולה is different because it is burned completely. So there is no reason to prefer it as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why would they not learn from voluntary שלמים? Because voluntary שלמים are common. Then they should also not learn from an obligatory עולה, because it is burned completely!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the challenge of step 9. Learning from an obligatory עולה has its own weakness, just as learning from voluntary שלמים does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might refuse to learn from voluntary שלמים because they are common, so they might have their own special rules. But an obligatory עולה also has a feature that obligatory שלמים lack: it is burned entirely on the מזבח. Each possible source differs in some way, so the alternative suggested in step 9 seems no better than learning from voluntary שלמים. This is only a temporary push-back; the next step answers it with a combined derivation that undoes רבי יצחק בר אבא's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
Common, frequently brought
Burned entirely on the מזבח
Because (it has this special feature)

steps.whatToRemember: Each single source has a weakness: voluntary שלמים are common (מצויין), and an obligatory עולה is burned completely (כליל). The next step resolves this by combining both sources.
steps.confusionAlert: 'שכן מצויין' and 'שכן כליל' are not new rules. Each one points out a difference that would block learning one offering from another. The גמרא shows that both sources have such a difference, so neither is better.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא מִשַּׁלְמֵי נְדָבָה דְּלָא גָּמְרִי —
phrases.english: What is different that they do not learn from voluntary peace-offerings?
Because they are common.
Then from an obligatory burnt-offering they should also not learn,
because it is burned entirely!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא מִשַּׁלְמֵי נְדָבָה דְּלָא גָּמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the alternative source proposed in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that בית הלל learn obligatory שלמים from obligatory עולה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Obligatory עולה has its own special feature (כליל, burned completely), just as voluntary שלמים have theirs (מצויין, common). So it is not a better source to learn from.

steps.title: Obligatory peace-offerings are learned from a combination of two sources
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that שלמי חובה are learned from both עולת חובה and שלמי נדבה together. So עולת חובה still needs its own פסוק even according to בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is derived from between the two of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection of step 10 and so upholds the challenge of step 9. Even though neither source works alone, בית הלל can learn the סמיכה of שלמי חובה by combining עולת חובה and שלמי נדבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source has a weakness: עולת חובה is burned completely, and שלמי נדבה are common. But each one covers the other's weakness, so the shared feature (both need סמיכה) carries over to שלמי חובה. This means עולת חובה is not learned from נדבה, so it still needs the פסוק 'כמשפט', and the ברייתא can follow בית הלל. רבי יצחק בר אבא's proof that it must follow בית שמאי falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes (is derived) from between them, a combination of two sources
The common feature, a method where two sources together prove a rule
Obligatory peace-offerings (e.g., the festival שלמים)
An obligatory burnt-offering (e.g., עולת ראייה)

steps.whatToRemember: שלמי חובה are learned from the two sources together (מבינייא), so even בית הלל need the פסוק 'כמשפט' for עולת חובה. The ברייתא does not have to follow בית שמאי.
steps.confusionAlert: The word אלא here does not cancel the derivation entirely. It replaces the single-source derivation that was just rejected in step 10 with a combined two-source derivation.

phrases.english: Rather, it is derived from between the two of them.
phrases.notes: Each source covers the other's weakness: 'burned completely' is answered by שלמי נדבה, and 'common' is answered by עולת חובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10's objection by offering a combined derivation. This sustains step 9's challenge and undoes רבי יצחק בר אבא's attribution of the ברייתא to בית שמאי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since neither עולת חובה nor שלמי נדבה works alone, בית הלל must learn everything from נדבה, so they would not need a פסוק for עולת חובה.
steps.terutzMaskana: שלמי חובה are learned from both sources together, so עולת חובה still needs 'כמשפט' even for בית הלל.

steps.title: Do בית שמאי really hold that obligatory peace-offerings need no סמיכה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the assumption that בית שמאי reject סמיכה for שלמי חובה. It cites רבי יוסי, who says both sides agree סמיכה is required. Their dispute was only about doing the שחיטה right after the סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do בית שמאי hold that obligatory peace-offerings do not need סמיכה? But it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יוסי said: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not disagree about סמיכה itself; both agree it is needed. What did they disagree about? About doing the שחיטה right after the סמיכה. בית שמאי say this is not necessary, and בית הלל say it is necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions the basic picture of the dispute. A ברייתא from רבי יוסי says בית שמאי also require סמיכה on שלמי חובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we assumed בית שמאי simply say no סמיכה is needed for שלמי חובה. רבי יוסי says the real dispute is about timing. For בית שמאי, the סמיכה can be done before יום טוב because it need not be right before the שחיטה. For בית הלל, it must be right before the שחיטה, so it has to be done on יום טוב itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaning one's hands on the head of an offering before it is slaughtered
The שחיטה must come immediately after the סמיכה
But it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a contradicting source)

steps.confusionAlert: Even according to רבי יוסי's version, בית שמאי do not do סמיכה on יום טוב. The reason is different, though: it can be done the day before, not that it is unnecessary.

phrases.english: And do Beit Shammai hold
that obligatory peace-offerings do not require placing of hands?
But isn't it taught: Rabbi Yosei said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree
about the placing of hands itself, that it is required.
About what did they disagree?
About slaughter immediately following placing of hands.
For Beit Shammai say: it is not necessary.
phrases.notes: So the סמיכה may be done before יום טוב.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say: it is necessary!
phrases.notes: So the סמיכה must be done on יום טוב itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי שַׁלְמֵי חוֹבָה לָא בָּעוּ סְמִיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the derivation question to the content of בית שמאי's position itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption (in the משנה and in the earlier discussion) that בית שמאי hold שלמי חובה need no סמיכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי's ברייתא reports that both schools agree סמיכה is required, and that they argue only about its timing.

steps.title: The משנה follows a different תנא's version of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. According to him, both sides agree the שחיטה must come right after the סמיכה, and they argue about whether סמיכה is needed at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (the תנא of our משנה) holds like this תנא. As it was taught: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה said: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not disagree that the שחיטה must come right after the סמיכה. What did they disagree about? About סמיכה itself. בית שמאי say it is not necessary, and בית הלל say it is necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by pointing to a second ברייתא that reports the dispute the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two תנאים who report the dispute differently. רבי יוסי says the dispute is about timing. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says it is about סמיכה itself. Our משנה, and the earlier discussion, follow רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, so the challenge does not apply to them.

keyTerms.meaning: In accordance with this תנא
רבי יוסי, son of רבי יהודה, a later תנא
Itself (the act of סמיכה as such)

steps.whatToRemember: There is a מחלוקת תנאים about what בית שמאי and בית הלל actually argued over: timing of the שחיטה (רבי יוסי) or סמיכה itself (רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה). Our משנה follows the second view.

phrases.english: He said it in accordance with this tanna,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: as it is taught: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree
about slaughter immediately following placing of hands, that it is necessary.
About what did they disagree?
About the placing of hands itself.
For Beit Shammai say: it is not necessary,
and Beit Hillel say: it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12 by attributing the משנה to a different תנא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution to a different תנא (מחלוקת תנאים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees with רבי יוסי that בית שמאי require סמיכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה disagrees, and our משנה follows him: בית שמאי do not require סמיכה on שלמי חובה.

steps.title: הלל הזקן brings his burnt-offering on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells how הלל הזקן brought his עולה to the עזרה on יום טוב to do סמיכה. The students of שמאי הזקן challenged him, and he avoided a fight by saying it was a female animal for שלמים. Then he swung its tail, and they left.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: There was an incident with הלל הזקן, who brought his עולה to the עזרה to do סמיכה on it on יום טוב. The students of שמאי הזקן gathered around him and said: What kind of animal is this? He said to them: It is a female, and I brought it as a שלמים offering. He swung its tail for them, and they went away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the basic dispute in the משנה and brings a story that shows it in real life. בית הלל allow bringing an עולה and doing סמיכה on יום טוב; בית שמאי do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה must be a male, so by saying 'it is a female,' הלל made the students think it was a שלמים. בית שמאי permit bringing שלמים on יום טוב. Swinging the tail kept them from checking closely. הלל, known for humility and peace, avoided a public argument in the בית המקדש while still acting on his own view.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a story brought as an illustration
The courtyard of the בית המקדש
What is its nature (what kind of animal is it)?
A female animal (cannot be an עולה)
He swung its tail (to hide whether it was male or female)

steps.confusionAlert: הלל was not doubting his own position. He brought a real עולה, following בית הלל. He only hid this to keep the peace with שמאי's students.
steps.whyThisMatters: The story shows that the dispute about bringing an עולה on יום טוב was practiced in real life. It also opens a longer narrative that continues on the דף.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
There was an incident involving Hillel the Elder,
who brought his burnt-offering to the Temple courtyard
to place his hands on it on a Festival.
The students of Shammai the Elder gathered around him

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מָה טִיבָהּ שֶׁל בְּהֵמָה זוֹ?
phrases.english: and said to him: What is the nature of this animal?
He said to them: It is a female,
phrases.notes: An עולה must be male, so this implies it is not an עולה.

phrases.english: and I brought it as a peace-offering.
He swung its tail for them,
phrases.notes: So they could not easily see whether it was male or female.

phrases.english: and they went away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussions about סמיכה, the גמרא returns to the core dispute of the משנה with a story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הלל הזקן acted on בית הלל's view by bringing an עולה and doing סמיכה on יום טוב, while concealing this to avoid conflict with בית שמאי's students.

steps.title: בית שמאי gain the upper hand that day
steps.stepSummary: After the incident with הלל, בית שמאי grew stronger than בית הלל and tried to fix the הלכה according to their view.
steps.simpleTranslation: On that day בית שמאי overpowered בית הלל, and they tried to establish the הלכה like their own opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues the הלל story and tells us what happened next. בית שמאי became dominant and wanted to set the הלכה their way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הלל had hidden that his animal was an עולה so he would not have to argue. People could read that as a sign that even הלל agreed you may not do סמיכה on an עולה on יום טוב. That gave בית שמאי the momentum to try to make their view the official הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Their hand grew strong. They gained the upper hand.
To fix or establish the official law.
Like them, meaning according to their opinion.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that הלל's peaceful sidestep had a cost. It almost caused the wrong הלכה to be set, and that sets up the rescue that comes next.

phrases.english: And on that day
phrases.notes: The day of the incident with הלל's animal.

phrases.english: the hand of Beit Shammai grew strong
over Beit Hillel,
and they sought to establish the halakha like them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם גָּבְרָה יָדָם שֶׁל בֵּית שַׁמַּאי עַל בֵּית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from Step 14 and shows the result of הלל's avoiding the confrontation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי became dominant that day and tried to fix the הלכה according to their view on סמיכה on יום טוב.

steps.title: בבא בן בוטא, a student of שמאי, steps in
steps.stepSummary: The story introduces בבא בן בוטא, a student of שמאי הזקן who knew the הלכה follows בית הלל, and tells us he sent for something.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an elder there, one of the students of שמאי הזקן, named בבא בן בוטא. He knew that the הלכה follows בית הלל, and he sent...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings in a new character who will push back against בית שמאי's move. This passage stops at the word 'and he sent', and the next passage tells us what he sent for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The surprise is that the person who defends בית הלל's view is himself a student of שמאי. He cared about the true הלכה more than about his own school's side. Here he is only introduced and begins to act. His full plan comes in the next part of the story.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain elder, meaning a respected senior scholar.
The students of שמאי the Elder.
The name of the elder who knew the הלכה follows בית הלל.
And he sent. The story continues on the next amud.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that a student of שמאי must side with בית שמאי. בבא בן בוטא came from שמאי's school, yet he knew the הלכה follows בית הלל and acted on it.

phrases.english: And there was a certain Elder there
of the disciples of Shammai the Elder,
and Bava ben Buta was his name,
who knew that the halakha is like Beit Hillel,
and he sent
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָיָה שָׁם זָקֵן אֶחָד מִתַּלְמִידֵי שַׁמַּאי הַזָּקֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces the figure who will push back against בית שמאי's attempt in Step 15 to fix the הלכה their way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בבא בן בוטא, a student of שמאי, knew the הלכה follows בית הלל and began to act to protect it.
